_meta.indication: Xiidra (lifitegrast ophthalmic solution) 5% is indicated for the treatment of the signs and symptoms of dry eye disease (DED).

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, prospective, double-masked, vehicle-controlled, parallel arm study; subjects randomized 1:1 to lifitegrast 5% or vehicle administered twice daily in each eye for 12 weeks, stratified by inferior corneal fluorescein staining score and eye dryness score at baseline.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult subjects with dry eye disease (DED) and a history of recent artificial tear use.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: mean change from baseline to Day 84 in the eye dryness score (EDS), a 0-100 point visual analogue scale (VAS).
pivotal_trials.result: Lifitegrast achieved a statistically significant improvement in mean change from baseline to Day 84 in eye dryness score vs vehicle: treatment effect 7.16 (SE 2.096), 95% CI (3.04, 11.28), p=0.0007.

nct_ctgov.title: A Study to Evaluate Efficacy and Safety of Lifitegrast in Subjects With Dry Eye (OPUS-3)

key_safety: The most common adverse reactions (incidence 5-25%) were instillation site irritation, dysgeusia and decreased visual acuity. Ocular treatment-emergent adverse reactions occurred in 46.2% of lifitegrast 5% subjects (N=1287) vs 21.2% vehicle (N=1177).
target_moa: Lifitegrast is a lymphocyte function-associated antigen-1 (LFA-1) antagonist that binds LFA-1 and blocks its interaction with intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1), which may be overexpressed in corneal and conjunctival tissues in dry eye disease.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary and there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion.

basis.text: The application was reviewed under Priority review designation.

summary.text: Xiidra was approved via a standard (non-accelerated) pathway under Priority review as a resubmission following a Complete Response letter dated October 16, 2015; the resubmission added the OPUS-3 study to provide substantial evidence of efficacy. The pediatric studies requirement under PREA was waived because dry eye disease rarely occurs in children, and the application was not referred to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: The application received a Complete Response letter dated October 16, 2015.
This Resubmission includes data from an additional clinical trial OPUS-3, as requested.
We are waiving the pediatric studies requirement for this application because necessary studies are impossible or highly impracticable. Dry eye disease rarely occurs in children.
The application received a Complete Response letter dated October 16, 2015.

basis.text: Substantial evidence of efficacy had not been provided in the NDA; findings from the Phase 2 Dry Eye, OPUS-1, OPUS-2 and SONATA studies were not sufficient to provide adequate evidence of efficacy.

Because the submitted studies did not fully support its efficacy, the original NDA submission received a Complete Response dated October 16, 2015. Findings from the Phase 2 Dry Eye, OPUS-1, OPUS-2 and SONATA studies were not sufficient to provide adequate evidence of efficacy for lifitegrast ophthalmic solution 5% in the twice daily dosing regimen for the treatment of dry eye disease.
